drug_class: Amino acid derivative / Homocystinuria treatment agent
purpose: Betaine is used to treat a rare inherited condition called homocystinuria, where harmful levels of an amino acid called homocysteine build up in the blood. High homocysteine can damage blood vessels, bones, and the eyes. This medication helps lower those levels to protect your body.
how_it_works: Your body normally converts homocysteine into a harmless substance, but in homocystinuria, this process does not work properly. Betaine acts as a helper by providing an alternative pathway to convert homocysteine into a safer amino acid called methionine. Think of it like opening a back door when the front door is blocked, so harmful buildup does not occur.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is nausea or an upset stomach. Some people notice a body odor change or a slightly unpleasant smell. You may also experience diarrhea or a decreased appetite. These side effects are usually mild.
warnings: A very important warning: if your homocysteine levels drop too low and methionine builds up too high, it can cause serious brain swelling called cerebral edema. Tell your doctor right away if you have severe headache, confusion, or vision changes. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to make sure your levels stay in a safe range. Always follow your diet plan alongside this medication.
typical_dosing: For adults and children over 3 years old, the usual starting dose is 3 grams taken by mouth twice a day. Your doctor may increase this dose based on your blood test results, sometimes up to 20 grams or more per day. The powder is dissolved in water, juice, or milk before drinking. Always take it exactly as your doctor tells you.
